document.abstract: This paper describe the world's first camera system that can capture images complying with the highest level image format specified in SMPTE 2036-1—(i.e., ultra-high definition television 2 [UHDTV2; 7680 × 4320/59.94 p, red, green, and blue (RGB) 4:4:4]). For this camera system, we developed a 33-megapixel complementary metal oxide semiconductor (CMOS) image sensor, an ultra-high-resolution lens, and a signal-processing function for correcting lens chromatic aberration in realtime. As a result, the limiting resolution of captured images was achieved over 4000 TV lines. Moreover, wavelength division (WDM) optical interface with nine 10-Gbit/s-serial digital interface (10G-SDI) modules was developed. Using this technology, the camera head and camera-control unit can be connected by a SMPTE 311 camera cable. In addition, the camera system's configuration and performance are also described.

authors.bio: Takayuki Yamashita joined NHK (Japan Broadcasting Corp.) in 1995 and has been engaged in research of HDTV cameras at NHK's Science and Technology Research Laboratories, since 1999. He is currently working on ultrahigh-definition TV camera systems. His research field includes the development of the image sensor and high-bandwidth digital signal processing. He is a member of the Institute of Image Information and Television Engineers of Japan.
authors.name: Takayuki Yamashita

authors.bio: Ryohei Funatsu joined NHK in 2002. Since 2004, he has been engaged in research of ultrahigh-definition TV camera systems at NHK Science and Technology Research Laboratories. His interest are in the development of high-definition image sensor and high-performance signal processing. Funatsu received B.E. and M.E. degrees in electrical and electronic engineering from Tokyo Institute of Technology in 2000 and 2002, respectively.
authors.name: Ryohei Funatsu

authors.bio: Tadaaki Yanagi joined Hitachi Denshi Technosystem Ltd. in 1989 and has been engaged in the development of high-definition/high-speed camera for Broadcasting at Hitachi Kokusai Electric Inc. He is currently working on ultrahigh-definition TV camera systems at the R&D division and in the Information System laboratories.
authors.name: Tadaaki Yanagi

authors.bio: Kohji Mitani is currently a senior engineer in the Engineering Administration department at NHK where he is engaged in the development of the ultra-high-resolution television system and HDTV broadcast equipment. — Mitani joined the Science and Technology Research Laboratories, NHK in 1987. Since then, he has been working on the solid-state image sensor and camera system. His experience in developing broadcasting cameras extends the range from the signal process in the analog and digital signal domain to the camera system for HDTV and high-resolution/high-frame-rate imaging. Since 1985, he has contributed and led the development of the Super Hi-Vision (SHV) system. — Mitani is a member of SMPTE, the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineering (IEEE), and the Institute of Image Information and Television Engineers of Japan.
authors.name: Kohji Mitani

authors.bio: Yuji Nojiri joined NHK in 1979. Since 1981, he has been engaged in research and development of HDTV, specifically, the HDTV laser beam film recorder, an HDTV standards converter, stereoscopic HDTV and extremely high-resolution imagery, and an ultrahigh-definition TV system at the NHK Science & Technology Research Laboratories. From 1999 to 2001, he worked for NHK Engineering Service Inc., and joined in the construction of YOKOHAMA Archives which is the TV program archives in Japan. Since 2011, he has been working for NHK Integrated Technology Inc. Nojiri received B.S. and M.S. degrees in electrical communication engineering and a Ph.D. in electrical engineering from Waseda University, Japan. He is a member of the Institute of Image Information and Television Engineers of Japan.
authors.name: Yuji Nojiri

authors.bio: Tetsuo Yoshida joined Shiba Denki in 1970 and has been engaged in development of high sensitivity/high speed camera for Broadcasting at Hitachi Kokusai Electric Inc. He is currently working on ultrahigh-definition TV camera systems at the R&D division in the Information System Laboratories.
authors.name: Tetsuo Yoshida
